title: Report Builder module in Jira Assistant
content:
The Report Builder in Jira Assistant (JA) designs reports made of tables, charts, text and layout components on top of data pulled from Jira, without writing code. Open it from Reports > Report Builder. The Report Builder home lists your saved reports and sample reports; start a new report from 'Create report', or open a sample and save it as your own.
A report is made of datasources (where the data comes from), parameters (values asked while running the report), variables, and components placed on the page. Reports can be previewed in the designer, opened in view mode, printed, exported as PDF and added to a dashboard as a gadget.
Works with Jira Cloud and Jira Data Center / Server.

title: Report Builder home and sample reports
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder home shows your saved reports and a gallery of sample reports grouped as Sprints & agile, Issue tracking, Time tracking, and Releases & epics. Samples include sprint status summary, sprint workload, issues by status with drill-down, open work by assignee with issue lists (a sub-report under each person), my open work, open issue aging, bugs by priority, created vs resolved, my and team timesheets, estimate vs actual, release scope and epic progress.
Opening a sample runs it in view mode with a banner. Samples ask for values such as projects, boards and sprints, user groups or a period. Use 'Save as my report' in the banner to keep it as your own report and change it in the designer. Saving a sample that embeds a sub-report also saves that sub-report as a report of your own, so it can be changed too.

title: Report Builder designer layout and panels
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder designer has the design area in the middle and docked panels on the sides: Toolbox, Datasource Explorer, Parameters, Variables, Global Fields and Functions on the left, Properties and Styles on the right, and the Console at the bottom.
Add a component by dragging it from the Toolbox, double-clicking it, or focusing it and pressing Enter. Drop components into a Columns Layout, Repeater, Tab Component or Canvas to place them inside it. Select a component to edit it in Properties; its toolbar moves, duplicates and deletes it, and Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) undo changes.
Panels can be resized by dragging their edge, pinned or set to auto-hide, and moved to the other side with the move button in the panel header or by dragging the header. The Console lists problems in the report, such as components without a datasource or names that are not valid; select a problem to open the item.

title: Report Builder datasources
content:
Datasources in the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder pull the data a report shows. Add one from the Datasource Explorer:
Jira issues (JQL): the issues of a JQL query with the fields you choose and an optional maximum. Sprint issues: the issues of sprints chosen now from agile boards, or from a Sprints parameter, with an optional extra JQL filter. Sprints: the sprints of boards in the chosen states (active, closed, future), optionally only the latest N. Worklogs: worklogs in a period (From and To are expressions, e.g. StartOf('month', Today())) of me, user groups, a users parameter or everyone. Jira lists: projects, issue types, statuses, agile boards, Jira fields, issue link types, my open issues or my user groups. Jira REST API: any Jira path starting with /rest/, with query parameters, headers and the path of the rows in the response.
Static table: rows typed in by hand. File / pasted data: a CSV, Excel or JSON file, or pasted CSV / JSON. Expression: rows built from an expression over parameters and other datasources, e.g. Distinct(Datasources.Issues, 'priority.name'). Derived: rows transformed from another datasource.
Insert parameter values in JQL with {{ expression }}, e.g. project in ({{ Parameters.projects }}); text values are quoted for you. 'Load fields' runs the datasource once and remembers its fields so they are offered in tables and charts.

title: Derived datasources and transform steps in the Report Builder
content:
A derived datasource in the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder starts from the rows of another datasource ('Derive from' in the Datasource Explorer) and runs steps in order: Filter rows, Add computed columns, Select / rename fields, Sort, Group & aggregate (count, count distinct, sum, average, median, minimum, maximum, first and last), Join datasource (inner, left, right or full; merge the fields or nest the matches as a list), Append datasources, Flatten nested list, Remove duplicates, Top N / paging, Pivot (values of a field become columns), Unpivot, and Running totals & ranking (row number, rank, running sum, running count, running average and more, optionally restarted for each group).
Each step explains what it is missing, steps can be moved up or down or removed, and the output fields are listed under the steps. Use 'Load fields' after a Pivot step so the new columns are offered in tables and charts.

title: Table component in the Report Builder
content:
The Table component of the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder shows the rows of a datasource. Data tab: the datasource, a Row Visible expression that hides rows, quick group by fields with a group footer (a row after each group with the total of every number column, shown with the column format; it is left out when the table has no number columns), and Pivot mode, which turns the rows into a cross table of a row field, a column field and an aggregated value field.
Columns tab: '+ fields' adds a column for every field; each column has a field, label, width, alignment, a format (e.g. =FormatNumber(Field.hours, 2)), a Visible expression, freezing while scrolling, conditional formatting rules (background, text colour, bold, italic when a condition is true) and cell content items such as links, images, menu icons, expressions or values that set a variable when clicked. Column groups put columns under a shared label, and columns can be moved up or down.
Rows tab: row groups (a parent group shows a header for each key and nests groups inside it; a details group lists rows) with filters, sorting, a group limit, group variables, footers and starting collapsed; plus head and footer rows with text or expressions spanning columns. Behavior tab: sorting by clicking a header, cell editing (changes only what the report shows), the Copy Data button, a drill-through variable and variables declared on the table.

title: Charts in the Report Builder
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder offers Bar, Horizontal Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, Polar Area, Radar, Scatter and Bubble charts, drawn with Chart.js.
Data tab: the datasource, the category / X field, the value / Y field (or a label and value field for pie, donut and polar charts, and a radius field for bubbles), an optional series field that makes one series per value, and the aggregation (sum, average, count, min, max, or none when the data is already one row per point). Other tabs set explicit series and colours, the title, subtitle and legend, the axes, styling such as bar sizes, line tension and chart height, the tooltip and when the chart is visible.
Every chart also carries its values as a table for screen readers.

title: Layout and other components in the Report Builder
content:
Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder components besides tables and charts: Header (level H1 to H6, anchor id, tooltip), Text, Image (source, alt text, size, object fit and a click URL), Horizontal Line (label, thickness, colour, style, margins), Columns Layout (1 to 6 columns side by side), Tab Component (tabs with their own components), Canvas (components placed freely with an X / Y position and size), Repeater (repeats its components once for each row of a datasource, with filter, sort, offset, limit, grid or inline layout, separators and an empty message) and Sub-report (embeds another saved report and passes it parameter values; it can be edited in place).
Header and text content can be static or an expression; switch with the fx button next to the field.

title: Report Builder parameters
content:
Parameters in the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder are values asked when the report runs. Add them from the Parameters panel. Types: Text, Masked Edit, Numeric, Date, Date Range, Dropdown, Multi-select, Autocomplete, Radio Button, Chips, Checkbox, File, and the Jira types Jira projects, Issue types, Statuses, Agile boards, Sprints, Jira users and User groups.
General tab: label, name (read as Parameters.name), description, type, width, Mandatory (the report waits for a value), Read Only, Hidden (the default value is used) and Allow Multiple, plus a default value. Values tab: options typed in or taken from a datasource (display and value field), placeholders, masks, number limits and date limits; a date range can have its own display format. Validation tab: length, pattern with its own message, key filter, number range, item counts and file types and size.
The report shows 'Enter the required parameters to run this report.' until every mandatory value is given; the parameters button changes them later. Saved reports and gadgets remember the values.

title: Expressions, variables and global fields in the Report Builder
content:
Expressions in the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder start with = in a field or are entered after switching the field to fx. They read Field.name (the current row, e.g. Field.status.name), Parameters.name, Datasources.name (the rows of a datasource), Variables.name and BuiltInFields.name, and use functions such as Concat, IIf, IfNull, IsNull, Count, Sum, Avg, Distinct, Join, First, Last, FormatNumber, FormatDate, FormatUserDate, Hours, IssueUrl, Today, StartOf, EndOf, Upper, Lower and Len.
The Functions panel lists every function by category with its parameters, their types, which are optional and their defaults, what it returns and examples; search it by name or by words of the description. The book button inside any expression field opens the same list and inserts the chosen function where you are typing. While a function is typed, the field shows its parameters and marks the current one. An unknown function or a wrong number of values is shown under the field and listed in the Console. The same list is on the product site as the Expression functions page.
Variables (Variables panel) hold values that change while the report is viewed, such as the row a reader clicked. Give them a name, scope, description and a default value (literal or =expression). A table cell item with the click action 'Set variable value' or 'Drill-through' changes a variable, e.g. clicking a status lists only its issues. Variables can also be declared on a table or text component.
Global Fields (BuiltInFields) are read-only values from the app: CurrentUserName, CurrentUserAccountId, CurrentUserEmail, CurrentUser, JiraUrl, DateFormat, TimeFormat, WorkingDays and MaxHoursPerDay.

title: Styles, page setup and global styles in the Report Builder
content:
In the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder, the Styles panel sets the typography, background, border, spacing, size and visibility (a checkbox or an expression) of the selected component.
Report Settings (toolbar) holds the title, description and version; the page size, orientation and margins used for the width of the report, printing and PDF; and Global Styles for the whole report: font, font size and text colour, the size, weight, colour and font of each heading level, and the header, body, alternate row and footer colours and cell border of tables. A component's own styles take precedence.

title: Previewing, saving, printing and sharing Report Builder reports
content:
In the Jira Assistant (JA) Report Builder, 'Preview' in the toolbar runs the report in the designer; the view button in the page header opens view mode. Save a report with a name of at least three characters; 'Save as' renames it or saves a copy, and the designer asks before leaving unsaved changes. Saved reports open from the home, the report picker or a bookmark and run straight away.
Print and 'Export as PDF' are in the viewer toolbar; the PDF is named after the report. Saved reports appear in the dashboard 'Add a Gadget' list and in the 'My Reports' gadget, which also exports selected reports as a .jrd file and imports .jrd files shared by others.
